Judge: In all four pairs the better frame (A in pair 1, B in pairs 2-4) wins clearly on all five criteria. None is close, and none is indistinguishable. The four weaker frames clearly come from one art kit (the same silver sedan, the same pastel-glass arcade, the same tower set with a ragged-crowned tower, the same peach mid-rise blocks), and they share systemic gaps. (1) The city is lifeless: streets and avenues carry almost no traffic, pedestrians, signals, streetlights, signage or clutter. (2) Lighting is even, high-key noon with weak aerial perspective and no time-of-day mood, so wide shots read as a massing model. The better frames use dusk, haze, sun flare, neon and lit windows. (3) Materials and assets fall short: hero cars have warped reflections and no contact shadows, roads look like plaza paving or bare asphalt with decals, towers are tiled-texture boxes, and the building kit is visibly copy-pasted. (4) Hero subjects lack motion cues; the helicopter has no readable rotor. (5) Wide fields of view bend the verticals, and the compositions lack foreground framing or a focal event. The weaker frames do have pleasant cumulus skies, a consistent warm sun direction and plenty of building mass in the aerials. Highest-leverage fixes: populate the streets with traffic, pedestrians and street furniture; add contact shadows and AO and fix the car paint reflections; add golden-hour or dusk lighting with distance haze and lit windows; add rotor blur; and break up the repetition in the building kit. Three of the better frames (the dusk neon street, the air-to-air helicopter shot and the sunset interchange) genuinely wow. The daylight car shot is convincing but not wow-level, and none of the weaker frames wows.
